Some stories start with a bang. This one starts with a whisper.

In The Quiet Frequency by Jules Rooke, retired spy Slade Quintz has spent years hiding at Cape Sorrow, a dead weather station on the foggy Oregon coast. His only company is Cipher, a Malinois with a bad hip from Kandahar, and Sebastion, a duct-taped concierge android who steeps tea he can't drink.

Then every machine Slade owns starts pulsing to the same rhythm. It's a voice: a dying colony of living light high above Earth, blacking out the grid every time it cries for help.

To answer it, Slade needs the woman he abandoned nine years ago. A storm is coming, and powerful people want that colony as a weapon.

It's a quiet, atmospheric, wry first-contact thriller with dry humor over real heartbreak. If you like burned-out spies and found-family sci-fi, it might be your next read.

Everyone else would hear static. But the man who can never stop hearing a whine is the first to notice the signal hiding inside it. It's a voice, from a dying colony of living light high above Earth, blacking out the grid every time it cries for help.

To answer it, Slade needs the woman he abandoned nine years ago. A storm is coming, and powerful people want that voice as a weapon.

Why did I write The Quiet Frequency?

Because I was tired of alien stories that start with explosions. I wanted one that starts with a whisper.

Slade Quintz is a retired spy hiding out at Cape Sorrow, a decommissioned weather station on the foggy Oregon coast. His roommates are Cipher, an aging Malinois with a bad hip, and Sebastion, a duct-taped hotel-concierge robot who steeps tea he can't drink. Then every machine Slade owns starts pulsing to the same rhythm.

It's a voice. A dying colony of living light, high above Earth, blacking out the grid whenever it calls for help. (Sebastion named it Lumen, since calling it 'it' seemed rude.)

Underneath the thriller, it's really a story about guilt, second chances, and how the hardest part of saving anything can be staying. I wanted dry humor sitting right on top of real heartbreak.

The Quiet Frequency is a science fiction thriller for readers of character-driven, wry first-contact sci-fi.
